gen-gf-goldman-fs-epilogue: Commanding and widely spaced, Goldman sets round, parenthesis-like forms along the line, with a lowercase that runs surprisingly large against its capitals. Epilogue then loosens the page with curvy, wire-like lines.
gen-gf-funnel-display-gf-cascadia-mono: Expressive and spaghetti-loose, Funnel Display draws every stroke at the same width. Cascadia Mono stands compact, its letters like pins in a wide board, so shrinking the heading would waste that loose swagger.
gen-gf-oxanium-switzer: Oxanium is all monoline strokes and a big, high-set lowercase. It makes a commanding statement, while Switzer, with its tubular, wire-like letters, is better at quietly carrying the text.
gen-gf-revalia-work-sans: A lowercase g with an open lower curve and widely separated letters give Revalia a relaxed, bold stride across the line. Loose stride up top, compass-steady Work Sans below: that mix is the draw.
gen-eater-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega reads friendly and modern, each letter looking bent from one length of tubing and every c visibly gapped. Pages of it would feel steady and easy-going, with Eater supplying the menace.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-julius-s: Ascenders that barely clear the x-height give Love Ya Like A Sister a low, level, bold, expressive beat. Julius Sans One lets it breathe, with spaced, open-ended curves throughout.
gen-dafont-nulshock-fs-merriweather-sans: Stretched, steady, unshaded: Nulshock spaces its capitals wide, barely taller than lowercase. Merriweather Sans then makes whole paragraphs feel sturdy, helped by an e with a clearly open eye.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-cascadia-mono: Scattered and commanding: Paprika fills the line with capital-sized lowercase. Cascadia Mono tucks in beneath as a compact, constant-weight hum, giving that loose top line something to lean on.
gen-gf-tektur-manrope: Tektur is expressive, with a pipe-cleaner look and oversized lowercase. It earns its keep big and brief, while Manrope, a sans with bright, open curves, handles the rest quietly.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-fs-fira-sans: Splayed and tube-like: Tilt Neon keeps one constant-width stroke. Fira Sans matches that no-contrast stroke and widens its s curves, so both carry a big x-height, which is where the two really connect.
